luna_triage.reason: The source re-tests the reported hyperstable vigilance pattern in an independent MDD cohort against healthy controls. The discussion explicitly treats the patient-control result as a qualified retest of that prior pattern. The sole supplied shipped original is the distinct iSPOT-D treatment-response paper (row 963), not the 2012 hyperstable-regulation paper.
luna_triage.omission_quote: The data from the NeuroPharm study showed no differences in the amount of similar EEG-vigilance stages; however, the data showed hyperstable vigilance profile for patients with MDD after accounting for changes in EEG-vigilance regulation.

luna_triage.reason: The source re-tests the reported EEG-vigilance discrimination between patients with major depression and healthy controls in an independent cohort. It explicitly frames the observed patient-control vigilance pattern as a qualified replication. The sole supplied shipped original is the distinct iSPOT-D treatment-response paper (row 963), not this 2012 diagnostic study.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Thus, the presented study showed that MDD patients were less likely to have decreasing vigilance over time compared to healthy controls. While this is not a straightforward replication, as previous studies focused on the percentage of vigilance stages, our findings still indicate an overall higher vigilance in patients.
